subject: Reserved capacity ask: sizing, swing clause, and GPU-cost sensitivity for Skyline
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@skyline.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Procurement <procurement@skyline.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — initial sizing and risk protection

Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week. Skyline is ready to move from pilot to a committed reserved model for inference. We want a 36-month construct, scale phased over Q3 and Q4, and care a lot about exposure if GPU market prices spike.

High level ask from procurement:
- Target baseline: 400 A100-equivalent GPU-days per day average (with burst windows).
- Start-of-term phasing: 60% in first 6 months, then ramp.
- We need a provision for quarterly swing (ability to reduce/increase by up to 25% each quarter).
- If third-party GPU pricing rises >15% vs. our signed benchmark, we need a negotiated pass-through or protection (discount floor).

Attached is our commitment request and procurement checklist for Redwood to review. Can you send back an initial capacity plan and a sensitivity view (what a 10/20/30% GPU-price move does to price per-token and to list discount needed)? Also propose any exec-credit or mitigation options Redwood can offer.

Appreciate a quick turn — procurement deadline for initial terms is July 6.

Jordan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Skyline AI

Attachment: Skyline_commit_request.pdf

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@skyline.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — initial sizing and risk protection

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. I attached a first-pass sizing workbook (redwood_capacity_initial.xlsx) that maps the 400 A100-eq baseline into A and B tier SKUs and shows cost per token under current market assumptions. Quick notes: 

- We can deliver a 36-month reserved construct with a phased ramp (60% H1 as you requested).
- Swing clause: we recommend +/-20% quarterly to balance planning certainty and runway. 25% is feasible but increases pricing risk materially unless paired with a small flexibility premium.
- Price protection: two options we typically offer:
  1) Indexation trigger: if a 3-month rolling GPU benchmark exceeds the baseline by X%, a pre-agreed price escalator/negotiation path kicks in.
  2) Price floor + executive credit: lock a discounted floor and offer a one-time executive credit if market moves exceed a high-water threshold.

I'll run a sensitivity grid for +10/ +20/ +30% GPU cost scenarios and share by Monday. Neha and Marcus are looped for commercial pricing and capacity-engine input. Could we get your expected traffic distribution (percentiles of seq lengths, steady vs burst windows) to refine the KV-cache and batching assumptions?

Available for a 30-min call Monday 6/24 10–11am PT if that works.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_capacity_initial.xlsx

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity ask — initial sizing and risk protection

Looping finance and ops: Jordan wants 36 months at ~400 A100-eq baseline with a requested +/-25% quarterly swing and a pass-through if GPU prices move >15%.

My read: pricing exposure at 25% swing + 30% market move yields large margin erosion unless we add either a flexibility premium or a shared-risk clause. Options to consider:

1) Tight swing (±20%) + concession: 12% up-front discount + $200k exec credit for any market shock >25% in a rolling quarter.
2) Wider swing (±25%) + indexation: add an indexation clause tied to an agreed cloud GPU benchmark; carve out a maximum annual pass-through of X%.
3) No swing but larger commit: lock 20% lower unit price for full 36 months and offer burst pool with fixed $/hour.

For analysis: Marcus please run the margin sensitivity (cost per token) for +10/20/30% GPU-cost scenarios for each option. Laura, flash CFO — do we have precedent for a $200k exec credit in recent reserve deals? If yes, what approvals needed?

— Avery

From: Jordan Lee <jordan@skyline.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Procurement <procurement@skyline.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — initial sizing and risk protection

Avery — thanks, that framing helps. A couple of follow-ups from procurement: 

- Skyline can accept ±20% swing but asks Redwood to allow one re-baseline per year to account for product seasonality.
- Procurement insists on a firm discount floor (we need clarity that unit price will not exceed X per token absent an index trigger).
- Regarding market shock: Skyline prefers an automatic mitigation (credit or discounted tranche) rather than a case-by-case negotiation. If you can codify the trigger and the remedy, that will shorten the procurement cycle.

Procurement attached their checklist and a short contract redline template. Deadline for signed commercial terms is July 12.

Jordan

Attachment: Skyline_procurement_checklist.docx

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — initial sizing and risk protection

Jordan — quick update after internal approvals. We can move forward with a middle-ground commercial that balances Skyline flexibility and Redwood unit economics. Summary of agreed commercial inputs we can commit to now (legal to draft language):

- Term: 36 months.
- Baseline: 400 A100-eq GPU-days/day average, phased 60% H1 then ramp.
- Quarterly swing: ±20% (Skyline may request one annual re-baseline).
- Price protection: three-part construct:
  a) Discount floor: a guaranteed floor rate of $0.0025 per token under normal market conditions.
  b) Index trigger: if the agreed GPU benchmark exceeds baseline by 12% (3-month rolling), an automatic mitigation path triggers — first a protected tranche discount for that quarter, then an executive credit review if >25% move.
  c) Executive credit: pre-approved up to $200,000 if a market shock >25% occurs in any rolling quarter; applies after protected tranche discount is exhausted.
- Flexibility premium: no up-front premium for ±20% swing. Wider swing requests will require a small capacity flexibility fee.

Attachments: proposal_summary_onepager.pdf (one-page commercial summary). I have Marcus and Laura on this thread — they confirmed the numbers and approvals. Next steps: legal will draft redlines this week and I’ll push the commercial summary + HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4721

Can you confirm procurement can accept the index trigger % and pre-approved credit? If yes, I’ll ask legal to prepare the redline set and DocuSign.

Thanks — Avery
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
